data.why: The dashboard has no upload route; it only browses a SQLite database that the repo's own simulator (app/simulator.py) populates from the repo's bundled samples/detections.json species list, so no files need to be copied or synthesized.

goals: Scan the activity timeline to see which bird species were automatically identified at the station over the last day
Open a species detail page to review its detection history, confidence trend, and daily activity for the past two weeks
Check a flagged or low-confidence detection's verification evidence to decide whether to trust an automated identification
Play back the audio clip tied to a specific detection to confirm the BirdNET call by ear
Build a life list to see which species have been confirmed at the station, sorted by first detection, most detections, or confidence
Check the device/status page to see recorder, BirdNET, storage, and queue health, including any failed recordings

review.summary: The tree describes this read-only BirdNET station dashboard faithfully: it covers every route and lays out the overview, filter, judge-one-detection, species, list and health stages, and the screens I sampled all show what their nodes claim. Before filing it needs a few corrections: the false 'no failed recordings / normal mode' data note, the 'confirmed species' wording, the left-out UTC-versus-local time mismatch, and tooltip actions whose cited screens show no tooltip.
